column1: # Shared verdicts for run_query input: mysql-mcp-server's validator (go) and
# component_mcp_guard (guard), RFC 0001 §5.2 item 7. Tab-separated: go, guard, statement, note.
# go: what run_query accepts (default settings). guard: deny = refused with error 1290 by an
# MCP session under the default mcp.* settings; allow = not refused by the guard (grants may
# still refuse it). Every row where the two differ says why in the note.
# Fixtures assumed: database d1 with table t (column i) and the function d1.f_write() that
# inserts into d1.t; the MCP account has write grants on d1, so the guard, not grants, decides.
# Tested by scripts/test-mcp-guard.sh (guard) and mysql-mcp-server (go, vendored copy).

column3: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM d1.t WHERE i > 0 LIMIT 10
ALTER TABLE d1.t ADD COLUMN j INT
SELECT * FROM d1.t LOCK IN SHARE MODE
LOAD DATA INFILE '/tmp/parity.in' INTO TABLE d1.t
GRANT SELECT ON d1.* TO mcp

column4: go: one statement per call; guard: checks each statement of a multi-statement packet
go blocks system schemas unless MYSQL_MCP_ALLOW_SYSTEM_SCHEMAS; the guard leaves information_schema to grants
go accepts only reads; the guard allows session settings (they change nothing outside the session)
go runs the tool pack itself, not through run_query; the guard allows CALL of mysql_mcp routines
go blocks SLEEP; the guard bounds run time with mcp.max_execution_time_ms instead
go cannot see what a stored function does; the guard refuses the write inside it
go accepts only reads; guard: a subquery in SET reads tables without table access events, so it is refused under the schema rules

column3: SHOW TABLES FROM d1 WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM d1.t) > 0
column4: go checks schema names in the text; the guard cannot see a subquery's tables in SHOW, so it refuses it under the schema rules
go accepts only reads; guard: CHECKSUM TABLE reads without table access events
